Axis: applicant
- Register: "Keli Electric Manufacturing (Ningbo) Co., Ltd."
- Document: "Keli Sensing Technology (Ningbo) Co., Ltd."

These are genuinely different company names: "Keli Electric Manufacturing" vs "Keli Sensing Technology". Both are Ningbo companies with "Co., Ltd." suffix, but the core names differ: "Electric Manufacturing" vs "Sensing Technology". Keli Sensing Technology (Ningbo) Co., Ltd. is a real company that makes load cells (R60 is the OIML recommendation for weighing load cells, so Keli Sensing Technology makes sense as the applicant for an R60 load cell certificate). "Keli Electric Manufacturing" appears to be a different entity name.

The rules: spelling drift, legal-suffix drift, accent differences = same-entity. Here the difference is not spelling drift — the actual company name words differ ("Electric Manufacturing" vs "Sensing Technology"). So this is genuinely different company names = different-entity, best_value = document's value, since the certificate is the legal instrument.

Also note the document text shows "Applicant: Keli Sensing Technology" (truncated in the excerpt), which supports the document value.

So verdict: different-entity, best_value: "Keli Sensing Technology (Ningbo) Co., Ltd.".

One caveat: the register value might be from extraction of a different certificate, but per the rules, the document is the legal instrument for this certificate id. So document wins.
